# Differential Diagnosis of PD, PSP, and MSA: An XGBoost Approach to Retinal Layer Analysis {.text-dark .mb-3}

**M. Rodriguez-Rubio¹, F.J. Martinez-Murcia¹, J. E. Arco², I. A. Illán¹, F. Segovia¹, C. Jimenez-Mesa¹, C. Vazquez-Garcia¹, J.M. Gorriz¹, J. Ramirez¹, S. Schönecker³, S. Kamp³, L. Klatte³, S. Katzdobler³, L. Marth³, O. Wagemann³, C. Palleis³, U. Fietzek³, E. Weidinger³, A. Danek³, G. Hölinger³, J. Havla³, A. Bernhardt³, A. Jäck³, J. Levin³**[cite: 1]

*¹Andalusian Research Institute in Data Science and Computational Intelligence (DaSCI), University of Granada, Spain | ²Mind, Brain and Behavior Research Center (CIMCYC), Granada, Spain | ³Department of Neurology, LMU University Hospital, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Munich, Germany*[cite: 1] {.text-secondary}

<!-- ================= 1. INTRODUCTION (RED BOX: 6 + 6 COLUMNS) ================= -->
::: {.bg-primary .text-white .p-5}
## 1. INTRODUCTION {.ugr-banner-title .text-white .mb-4}

::: {.grid style="--bs-gap: 24mm;"}
::: {.g-col-6}
**Clinical Challenge:** Parkinson's disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA) share overlapping clinical presentations in early stages, making differential diagnosis challenging[cite: 1].

**Underlying Proteinopathies:** PD and MSA are characterized by alpha-synuclein aggregation (**synucleinopathies**), whereas PSP involves pathological tau deposition (**tauopathy**)[cite: 1].
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
**The Retina as a Window to the CNS:** Optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables precise, non-invasive quantification of individual retinal layers, reflecting pathology-specific thinning patterns[cite: 1].

**Objective:** We present a systematic machine learning evaluation using **XGBoost** across four classification tasks to distinguish healthy controls, proteinopathic groups, and clinical subtypes from OCT retinal morphometry[cite: 1].
:::
:::
:::

<!-- ================= 2. METHODOLOGY (CSS GRID: 7 + 5 COLUMNS) ================= -->
::: {.section-container}
## 2. METHODOLOGY {.ugr-title .mb-3}

::: {.grid .align-items-start style="--bs-gap: 20mm;"}

<!-- Left Column (7 of 12 columns) -->
::: {.g-col-7}
Macular records were acquired and segmented using the **Heidelberg Spectralis OCT** device[cite: 1]. Only baseline high-quality visits per patient were included, averaging both eyes to represent bilateral neurodegenerative involvement[cite: 1]. A total of **29 morphometric features** were extracted, normalized at the subject level by total macular volume ($\text{TMV}+Z$), and standardized ($Z\text{-score}$).

::: {.border .p-3 .my-4 .bg-white .text-center .mx-auto style="width: 88%;"}
![](images/oct_segmentation.jpg){style="width: 100%; max-height: 60mm; object-fit: cover;"}

*<strong>Fig 1.</strong> Automated segmentation of macular retinal layers (RNFL, GCL, IPL, INL, OPL, ONL, RPE) via OCT.*[cite: 1] {.text-secondary .mb-0 .mt-2 style="font-size: 20pt; text-align: center;"}
:::

<!-- Tasks Subcolumn (7 of 12) -->
::: {.g-col-7}
Classification was conducted using the **eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)** algorithm evaluated via repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation ($10 \times 5\text{-fold}$ CV)[cite: 2].

**Four Diagnostic Tasks Evaluated:**[cite: 1, 2]

* **HvP:** HC ($N=36$) vs. Parkinsonism ($N=98$)[cite: 2].
* **SvT:** Synucleinopathies (PD+MSA, $N=64$) vs. Tauopathy (PSP, $N=34$)[cite: 2].
* **3-Class (3C):** PD vs. PSP vs. MSA ($N=98$)[cite: 2].
* **4-Class (4C):** HC vs. PD vs. PSP vs. MSA ($N=134$)[cite: 2].
:::
:::
:::

<!-- Right Column: Dark Side Box (5 of 12 columns) -->
::: {.g-col-5 .bg-dark .text-white .p-5}
### 2.1 DATASET AND PARTICIPANTS {.ugr-subtitle .text-white .mb-3}

From 488 initial records (186 participants), individuals with low-quality estimations or missing values were discarded, resulting in **134 subjects**[cite: 1]:

| Group | $N$ | Age (mean±SD) | M/F |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **HC** | 36[cite: 1] | $63.6 \pm 9.9$[cite: 1] | 20 / 33[cite: 1] |
| **PD** | 46[cite: 1] | $59.5 \pm 13.0$[cite: 1] | 29 / 19[cite: 1] |
| **PSP** | 34[cite: 1] | $70.4 \pm 7.5$[cite: 1] | 20 / 17[cite: 1] |
| **MSA** | 18[cite: 1] | $59.0 \pm 7.6$[cite: 1] | 20 / 9[cite: 1] |

<p class="mt-4 mb-0" style="font-size: 21pt; color: #D1D5DB;">Nine macular layers were segmented (RNFL, GCL, IPL, INL, OPL, ONL, RPE)[cite: 1], alongside inner/outer retinal layer aggregates (IRL, ORL), total macular volume (TMV), ETDRS grid ring zones, and the RNFL-to-NT ratio[cite: 2].</p>
:::

<!-- Right Column: Summary Table (7 of 12 columns) -->
::: {.g-col-7 .table-results}
### Classification Performance Summary (Mean ± SD, $10 \times 5\text{-fold}$ CV)[cite: 2] {.fw-bold .mb-3 style="font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 28pt;"}

| Task | Norm. | Set | Accuracy | Bal. Acc. | F1-Macro |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **HvP** (HC vs. Rest)[cite: 2] | $Z$[cite: 2] | *raw*[cite: 2] | **$0.724 \pm 0.079$**[cite: 1, 2] | $0.609 \pm 0.064$[cite: 2] | $0.619 \pm 0.073$[cite: 2] |
| **SvT** (PD+MSA vs. PSP)[cite: 2] | $\text{TMV}+Z$[cite: 2] | *raw*[cite: 2] | **$0.704 \pm 0.057$**[cite: 1, 2] | $0.650 \pm 0.071$[cite: 2] | $0.652 \pm 0.071$[cite: 2] |
| **3-Class** (PD/PSP/MSA)[cite: 2] | $\text{TMV}+Z$[cite: 2] | *raw*[cite: 2] | **$0.521 \pm 0.100$**[cite: 1, 2] | $0.472 \pm 0.105$[cite: 2] | $0.440 \pm 0.111$[cite: 2] |
| **4-Class** (HC/PD/PSP/MSA)[cite: 2] | $Z$[cite: 2] | *raw*[cite: 2] | **$0.395 \pm 0.120$**[cite: 1, 2] | $0.374 \pm 0.110$[cite: 2] | $0.354 \pm 0.112$[cite: 2] |

::: {.bg-light .border-start .border-primary .border-5 .p-3 .mt-3}
**Impact of TMV Normalization:** Including subject-level TMV normalization ($\text{TMV}+Z$) specifically enhanced the separation of symptomatic cohorts, boosting **SvT** accuracy from $0.622 \pm 0.065$ ($Z$) to **$0.704 \pm 0.057$** ($\text{TMV}+Z$)[cite: 2].
:::
:::

:::

<!-- ================= 4. KEY FINDINGS (RED BOX: 6 + 6 COLUMNS) ================= -->
::: {.bg-primary .text-white .p-5}
## 4. KEY FINDINGS & CONCLUSIONS {.ugr-banner-title .text-white .mb-4}

::: {.grid style="--bs-gap: 24mm;"}
::: {.g-col-6}
* **Robust Biological Stratification ($\approx 70\%$):** The XGBoost framework effectively distinguishes synucleinopathies (PD+MSA) from tauopathies (PSP) ($0.704 \pm 0.057$), comparable to binary HC vs. pathology discrimination ($0.724 \pm 0.079$)[cite: 1, 2].
* **Divergent Retinal Signatures:** Findings confirm that alpha-synuclein and tau pathology exert divergent neurodegenerative pressures on inner and outer retinal architecture[cite: 2].
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
* **Multiclass Phenotypic Overlap:** Performance in 3-class ($0.521$) and 4-class ($0.395$) settings highlights the significant morphological and clinical overlap between PD and MSA[cite: 1, 2].
* **Clinical Translation:** Combining OCT biomarkers with machine learning paves the way for faster, non-invasive, and cost-effective early-stage stratification in atypical parkinsonism[cite: 1, 2].
:::
:::
:::
